My field isn't in health, but my understanding is that 19g of the carbs aren't digestible.

Fiber and Erythritol (a sugar alcohol) are non-digestible and don't effect blood sugar. So while they are carbs, they can be considered non-carbs from the standpoint of blood sugar impact. So taking away the 17g fiber and 2g erythritol as non-carbs, you're left with 3g "net" carbs that actually impact blood sugar.

DISCLAIMER: This is my understanding. I do not claim absolute knowledge and am open to criticism and correction if I've misunderstood!
